classification.difficultyReason: Generate the four missing face-connected arrangements while excluding rotations and mirror duplicates, including configurations extending in three dimensions. Then test for uniform cross-section in any orientation to distinguish the two non-prisms.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw four other objects that can be made from four cubes stuck together as described in Question 3b: each cube has at least one face stuck to the face of another cube. Only one version of each object needs to be drawn on isometric paper. Three of them have been drawn for you here. Count mirror images as the same object.

spec.description: Four cubes in a single-level two-by-two square on isometric dots.
spec.mathematics: One of the three supplied tetracubes.

spec.description: Four cubes in a straight single-level row on isometric dots.
Single-level L of four cubes, three along one arm and two along the other including the shared corner.
Isometric drawing space for four additional solids.

answer.short: The four additional objects are shown. There are seven objects altogether, counting rotations and mirror images as the same object.
answer.worked: Count mirror images as the same object. Besides the supplied straight, square and L arrangements, draw a planar T, a planar zigzag, a three-dimensional bent chain and a three-dimensional corner arrangement. Each contains four cubes joined face to face.

spec.description: Planar T and zigzag, skew four-cube chain, and three-dimensional corner tetracube.
spec.mathematics: Four missing free tetracubes; reflected skew chain treated as the same source object.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many of these objects were not prisms?

answer.worked: The five planar arrangements are prisms, because each is an extrusion of its footprint. The three-dimensional bent chain and corner arrangement do not have a uniform cross-section, so 2 are not prisms.
